question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw-authored external-content wrappers by default, or should this be exposed as a new captureFilter configuration option?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent security boundary determines whether trust is framework-owned by default or delegated to operator configuration, and that choice should not be made by cleanup automation.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/tool content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented operator-controlled excludeWrapped option, with schema, manifest, docs, and tests showing upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Fold into broader provenance work
options.body: Defer this narrow filter until the memory trust/provenance model in related open issues defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/tool content.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the external-content marker hardening path and is a plausible reviewer for a security-boundary choice that crosses memory and wrapper semantics.
